grh_0799a34520be21bb3b90.title: A Friend in Need
paragraphs: Britt encounters his old friend Art Hamper, a fugitive accused of murdering Clyde, the foster brother he had once considered as close as blood. Art insists he was framed by circumstances surrounding their inheritance, and Britt initially believes him enough to help arrange a surrender. The sheriff's evidence shows that Art's story is a lie, but Britt still gives him a chance to come in peacefully. Art instead tries to use Britt to escape and fires on him, only to be fatally shot by a lawman; dying, he apologizes for lying to the friend he betrayed.

grh_07b2d714b02169505efe.title: Words at War 43-11-02 (21) Here Is Your War
paragraphs: A dramatized selection from Ernie Pyle's Here Is Your War presents his ground-level view of the North African campaign. Instead of following one plot, it moves through scenes of dirty camps, infantry marches, delayed letters from home, exhausted soldiers, combat deaths and brief moments of humor. Pyle emphasizes the ordinary men who carried the campaign and the gulf between their experience and life at home, ending with the North African fighting over and rows of white crosses left behind as the army prepares to move on to the next battlefield.

grh_07664f7ff036b59becb3.title: Mad Interlude
paragraphs: Successful businessman Hector Travis has worked without a real break for thirty years while his partner, wife and children continually add demands for money, possessions and plans. Suddenly he locks himself in his room, talks nonsense and behaves as though he has lost his mind, throwing both family and business into confusion. Dr. Christian eventually explains that Hector is not ill at all: completely worn down and unable to ask for rest any other way, he has been pretending to be crazy so the treadmill will stop. His family finally understands what their expectations have cost him and promises not to drive him that hard again.
